buyer.label: Chicago
buyer.// finance: What the car costs per month, which is the number this buyer actually decides on. A promo applies ONLY to a certified car of its own model — a non-CPO i5 finances at fallback_apr like anything else. Past its expires date a promo stops applying and the page says so; it is never silently kept alive. fallback_apr is a real rate that drifts: fallback_checked is when it was last verified, and the page warns when that goes stale.

fees.tax_note: Illinois taxes a vehicle at the BUYER's home rate wherever it is bought, so this applies to every car on the page, not just the local ones. Chicago/Cook combined — verify against the current rate before trusting a total.

// years: One EV per brand, model year 2024 and newer. The rule lives HERE and nowhere else: years resolves trim <- model <- brand <- defaults like every other parameter, and it used to be written out once per model, which is four places for one decision to rot. The range runs to 2027 because "2024 and above" has no upper bound and 2027 cars list in 2026 — every range this replaced stopped at 2026 and would have excluded them in silence.
// national_only: The long tail asks the country AND the buyer's states, both. It asked only the country until the overlap log had enough days to settle it, and the answer was not the one sources_for()'s comment assumes: over 28 recorded observations the States query found 310 cars and 232 of them were invisible to National. Split by the only thing that governs it -- how big a catch the National query is allowed -- a depth=full target (~100 cars nationally) loses 21% by going national_only, and a depth=light one (20 cars, the whole country, cheapest first) loses 88%. All 28 of the LONG-TAIL TARGETS are light -- a different 28 from the 28 observations above, which is why this says which --  so their National query returns the twenty cheapest of that model IN AMERICA. The split is measured on the light targets the log could see and applied to these by depth: source_overlap() needs two sources to compare, so a national_only target cannot contribute an observation and not one of these is in the window. Paid for out of cadence, not budget: 10 -> 15 days buys the second source at 913 calls/month against 1000 and a worst day of 38 against 40, and 15 keeps plan_horizon() at 60 days where 13 and 14 push it to 156 and 84. The cost is real and is freshness: twice a month instead of three times. bmw-i5-cpo keeps national_only and is not part of this -- a nationwide certified watch is national BY DEFINITION, not to save a call.
// legacy_ids: Old target ids -> new ones, so history carries over when the config is restructured. A NULL value means the opposite and is not an omission: the rows are known about and deliberately left orphaned. lucid-air-touring and -grand-touring merged into one trimless lucid-air, and 53 of the 68 rows they hold are model year 2022 or 2023 — measured, not assumed — which the 2024+ watchlist can never return again, so remapping them would publish 53 cars as current inventory that no query on this sheet could produce. chevrolet-equinox-ev-rs is the opposite case on every axis: 0 of its 31 rows are pre-2024 and its window was a SUBSET of the new target's, so its reconstructed cut-off is narrower than the truth rather than wider, which is conservative. It is mapped. bmw-i7 is one row from 2026-08-29, written when the i7 was briefly trimless, and it carries no trim at all — there is no trim target to map it to, so it stays where it is.

cpo.label: CPO under 30k mi
cpo.note: Stood down BEFORE IT EVER RAN, on a prediction rather than a measurement — which is the honest way to say this and the first version of this note did not. It was added at 02:38 on 2026-09-01 with offset 1 on a cadence of 2, so its first due day was 2026-09-02: it never fetched once and never billed a call. The 30 calls a month it would have cost is a plan figure, not a spend. What is measured is the mechanism: the query takes the 40 lowest-mileage i7s in the country on miles.asc and then filters to certified under 30,000 miles, and in the i7 rows actually observed, ranks 1-42 are 2026 cars at 1-14 miles — new inventory, none certified — so the first certified i7 sits below the window. The i5 version of the same recipe returns cars, and its one structural difference is years [2024, 2025], no current model year. Dropping 2026 here may well fix it, and that is worth two calls to find out; it is not a target that cannot work, it is a target not worth 30 calls a month on this shopping list while the ordinary edrive50 query already holds certified sub-30k i7s. One flag brings it back.
